title: What is known about 1RB0RD_1LC0RA_1LF1LD_0RE0LC_---1LB_1RB1RC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RD_1LC0RA_1LF1LD_0RE0LC_---1LB_1RB1RC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, and it is now a question about a small system of events, proved in Lean. The machine is a counter ticked once per round trip across a growing wall, and the tick is a carry automaton on the counter's digits. When a carry runs through all the digits it reads the last cell, and one of four things happens, each proved for every wall and every digit string: the last cell is set, the counter gains a digit, the whole wall is turned into counter digits, or the machine halts. So the machine halts from blank tape exactly when this event system reaches a halting event (kernel only). In the run from blank tape the first such event comes about 1.96·1020 steps in and turns a wall of 8,072,508,833 pairs into digits; the next one is of the order of 22.5·109 sweeps later, and which kind it is is not known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 36,723 cells have been visited and 18,406 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The wall's round trip
claims.text: From D leaving the counter, 0^inf (10)^n D> 1 R, the head crosses the wall, adds one pair at the blank end and comes back: 0^inf (10)^(n+1) A> 0 R after 6n + 4 steps, for every n and every tape R. Built from the three pieces wall_right, wall_left, left_end.

claims.title: A whole sweep that sets x1
claims.text: When the counter's first digit x1 is 0: 0^inf (10)^n 1 0 A> 1 1 0 1 R reaches 0^inf (10)^(n+2) A> 1 1 1 1 R in 6n + 18 steps: x1 becomes 1, the wall grows by one pair, and A is back at x0.

claims.title: The carry's zigzag
claims.text: Over a stretch of ones the carry moves right three cells per 7 steps: L 1 0 0 D> (111)^n R reaches L (110)^n 1 0 0 D> R.

claims.title: A sweep is one step of the carry automaton, for every digit string
claims.text: An arrival 0^inf (10)^(n+1) A> 1 1 x1 1 ... xk 1 R reaches 0^inf (10)^(n+2) A> 1 1 y1 1 ... yk 1 R whenever the automaton (a: 0→1 stop, 1→0 b; b: 0→1 a, 1→0 c; c: 0→0 c, 1→1 a) stops inside the digits and turns xs into ys. This holds for every n, every digit string and every tape R. The proof is by induction over the digits, chaining symtm rules for each state and digit on the way right and each pending pair on the way back.

claims.title: Halting only at end events
claims.text: If no sweep ever runs off the end of the digits, the machine never halts from that arrival. Along any number of sweeps that stop inside the digits, halting is unchanged.

claims.title: The first arrival
claims.text: From blank tape, step 30,225 is the arrival with a wall of 10 pairs and the 109 digits X0, followed by a last cell 1. The list simulator is evaluated by the kernel.

claims.title: 8,072,508,823 sweeps without reaching the end
claims.text: The automaton becomes a transducer on words of generators, and ak is kept as a straight-line program of 6,010 nodes. The checker's soundness is proved in Lean, and the certificate of 7,351 entries is checked by compiled code. The result: all 8,072,508,823 sweeps after the first arrival stop inside the digits, ending with the digits Y0.

claims.title: The automaton permutes digit strings
claims.text: Digit i of a sweep's result depends only on digits 1..i, and on the strings of each length up to 12 the automaton is a bijection whose cycles all have power-of-two lengths: an odometer-like map. Deep carries are rare: the first sweeps reaching x40, x70, x100 come 1,635, 402,291 and 69,230,963 sweeps after step 2·10<sup>7</sup>.

claims.title: The first end event does not halt; halting reduces to one configuration
claims.text: The next sweep runs into the last cell in state b and passes it without halting. It then comes back across the whole wall, turning each pair 10 into 11, and reaches post n = C> 1 (11)^n R1; the kernel checks this for every wall n. Together with the claims above: the machine reaches post 8072508832 from blank tape, about 1.96·1020 steps in, and it halts from blank tape if and only if it halts from there.

claims.title: Every end event, for every counter
claims.text: The counter is the digits x1..xk, each followed by a separator 1, then a last cell d with blank tape after it. When the carry runs through all the digits and reads d: in state a, d = 0 becomes 1, and d = 1 gives the counter one more digit; in state b on 0 or state c on 1 the machine halts; in state b on 1 or state c on 0 the pass back runs one cell out of step and turns the wall of n + 1 pairs into digits, leaving a wall of one pair and the digits 1<sup>n</sup> 0 marks 1, where the marks are 1 after each digit that left the carry in state c. Each case holds for every wall and every digit string, and each leaves a counter of the same shape.

claims.title: The machine is the event system
claims.text: evstep is one sweep as a map on (wall, digits, last cell), with no value when the sweep halts. From any arrival of this shape the machine halts if and only if iterating evstep reaches a halting event; from blank tape, if and only if it does so from a wall of 10 pairs, the 109 digits X0 and last cell 1.

claims.title: After the first end event
claims.text: The first end event of the run from blank tape is a conversion (state b on the last cell 1). The machine reaches the arrival with a wall of one pair and a counter of 8,072,508,943 digits: 8,072,508,832 ones, a 0, the 109 marks of the last carry and a 1. It halts from blank tape if and only if the event system halts from there. The certificate of the 8·10<sup>9</sup> sweeps before the event is checked by compiled code; the event itself by the kernel.

claims.title: The event system against the machine
claims.text: The Python copy of evstep gives the same next arrival, or the same halt, as the machine itself on 20,000 random arrivals with walls of 1 to 7 pairs and up to 12 digits, covering every kind of event.

claims.title: The mirrored table is the same event system
claims.text: 1RB1RE_1LC1LA_1RA0LD_1LC0LE_0LF0RA_---1RC (bbchallenge 132695) is this table in a mirror with the states renamed. Its run from blank tape is this machine's run from blank tape started in state C, which reaches an arrival after 16 steps, so it halts if and only if the event system halts from a wall of one pair, the single digit 1 and last cell 1. The two machines are separate halting questions: the same event system from two different counters.

claims.title: What end events do on other counters
claims.text: Observed, not proved. From 300 random counters of 30 to 60 digits, followed to the first halt or conversion, 170 end in a halt and 130 in a conversion. From the counter after the first end event with a stand-in wall of 1 to 30 pairs in place of 8,072,508,833, 7 end in a halt and 23 in a second conversion, after 4·10<sup>9</sup> to 10<sup>13</sup> sweeps. The outcome changes with the stand-in wall with no visible pattern, so this says nothing about the real run.

claims.title: The next end event is beyond simulation
claims.text: After the conversion the first sweep runs through the 8·109 ones and leaves the counter starting with 001 repeated 2.7·109 times. On the stand-in runs the number of sweeps to the next end event doubles about every 3 digits, which puts the real one at the order of 22.5·109 sweeps. Which state the carry is in then is a question about the automaton group generated by a = (e, b)σ, b = (a, c)σ, c = (c, a) on an almost periodic string.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts if and only if the event system reaches a halting event from the counter after the first end event. That needs the carry to read the last cell in state b on a 0 or in state c on a 1.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1RE_1LC1LA_1RA0LD_1LC0LE_0LF0RA_---1RC up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet, but we know exactly what it is doing. This machine is a counter: a stretch of digits at the right end of the tape, ticked once every time the head makes a round trip across a long, growing wall of 10s. The tick is a carry, like adding one, but in a strange number system with three carry states. Whether the machine halts is decided at the rare moments when a carry runs through every digit: Lean proves what each such moment does, and one kind of moment halts.

facts.text: One sweep is one step of the carry automaton, and every end event is one of four cases, proved in Lean for every wall and digit string.
From blank tape, proved without any computation beyond the kernel.
The first end event: a wall of 8,072,508,833 pairs becomes counter digits. No halt before it.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.491). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 36,723 cells (26,953 left of the start, 9 right), with a density of 1s of 0.501.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A wall and a counter
html: After the first 40,000 steps the tape has two parts. On the left is a wall: n copies of 10. On the right, fixed in place, is a counter of 221 cells: a digit on every even cell and a 1 on every odd cell, x0 1 x1 1 x2 1 ... x110, with x0 = 1.

The head bounces. State A runs right across the wall (two steps per pair), does some work in the counter, then D, C and F run back left (four steps per pair). At the blank end the wall gains a pair and A turns back. A round trip costs 6n + 4 steps, proved in Lean for every n (round). Because the wall gains one pair per trip, N trips take about 3N2 steps: the left end of the tape grows like the square root of the time, while the right end, the counter, stays put.

sections.heading: Each trip adds one, in a strange number system
html: Each time A arrives at the counter, the digits x1, x2, ... change by a carry rule. It is a finite automaton that reads the digits from x1 rightwards, rewriting each one:

carry statedigit 0digit 1
a (start)write 1, stopwrite 0, go on in b
bwrite 1, go on in awrite 0, go on in c
cwrite 0, go on in cwrite 1, go on in a

State a alone would be ordinary binary counting: flip trailing 1s to 0 until a 0 becomes 1. States b and c make the carry travel further and in a more tangled way. The rule was read off the machine and checked against it on every trip of the first three million steps.

It behaves like an odometer: digit i of the result depends only on digits 1 to i, and on strings of any fixed length the rule is a permutation whose cycles have lengths 1, 2, 4, 8, ... So the low digits cycle quickly and the carry reaches deep digits only rarely: x40 first changes 1,635 trips after step 2·107, x70 after 402,291 trips, x100 after 69 million.

sections.heading: What happens when the carry runs through every digit
html: The counter has 110 digits; beyond x110 the tape is blank. Each sweep starts the carry at x1, so to know when the carry first reaches the end you have to iterate the automaton about 8·109 times. That is a minute of plain computation. It can also be done exactly in a fraction of a second: write the automaton's states as group elements (a = (e, b)σ, b = (a, c)σ, c = (c, a)) and keep the huge power ak as a straight-line program, a table of a few thousand pieces each made of two earlier ones. Lean checks a certificate for that table. The first 8,072,508,823 sweeps after step 30,225 all stop inside the digits.

The next sweep, starting from a wall of 8,072,508,833 pairs about 1.96·1020 steps in, runs through all the digits and reads the last cell in state b. What happens at such a moment depends only on the carry's state and on the last cell, and Lean proves each case for every length of wall and every digit string:

carry state at the last celllast cell 0last cell 1
athe cell becomes 1the counter gains a digit
bhaltsthe wall becomes digits
cthe wall becomes digitshalts

From blank tape the first such moment is state b on a 1. The machine does not halt. It writes one new cell, and on its way back, one cell out of step, it turns every separator into a digit and every pair 10 of the wall into 11. The old wall has become eight billion new counter digits, all ones, followed by a 0 and by marks that record where the last carry was in state c. A new wall of one pair starts at the left end.

Every case leaves a counter of the same shape, so the table is the whole story: the machine halts from blank tape exactly when this little system of events reaches a halting entry (blank_halts_iff_events, checked by Lean's kernel alone).

What is not known is which entry comes next. The first sweep after the conversion runs straight through the eight billion ones, leaving 001 repeated, and then the carry has to work its way through all of that again. On small stand-ins for the wall the wait doubles about every three digits, so the real second event is of the order of 22.5·109 sweeps away. With stand-in walls of 1 to 30 pairs, 7 runs end in a halt and 23 in a second conversion (observed, not proved), with no pattern that would tell us the answer for the real wall.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: A counter beside a growing wall of 10s, ticked once per sweep by a carry automaton. Lean proves every end event for every counter (set the last cell, add a digit, turn the wall into digits, or halt), so the machine halts exactly when a small event system does. The first end event, about 2·10^20 steps in, turns a wall of 8·10^9 pairs into digits; which kind the next one is is not known.
family: automaton counter beside a growing wall
